_comment: Written by the trading runs (9:30a / hourly / 3:30p ET). Never contains account numbers, broker IDs, or any account other than the sandbox.

account.note: Cash account. Proceeds settle T+1. Re-read live at 11:22 ET from the broker and unchanged for the third read running: 128.90 total, all of it cash, nothing unsettled, so deployable is the full balance. No equity or option positions are open, which is why the second mid-session run also had no exit to enforce.

entryWatch.trigger: Reaction strong and still holding 30-60 min after the 8/5 open
entryWatch.why: Resolved against, and each hour has made it more so. AMD is bid 482.06 at 11:22 ET against a 518.58 official close, about -7.0%, below both the 491.73 open bid and the 486.55 read an hour ago. A continuation setup needs a strong reaction to continue; this reaction is negative and has deteriorated at every read today. Nothing about a stand-aside branch is revisited because the loss widened - it was already dead at 10:22 - but a thesis moving further from valid on every read is worth stating plainly rather than leaving as 'unchanged'.

entryWatch.trigger: Reaction strong but the leader is already extended
entryWatch.why: Conditional on a strong leader, and the leader printed red and kept going. There is no upside chain to find a laggard in. SMCI, the name this read pointed at, is bid 30.94 and down about 2.4%, worse than the 31.01 and -2.1% an hour ago - it is not lagging a move, it is following the same one down.

entryWatch.trigger: A pullback that holds on 8/6 or 8/7, not today's reaction bar
entryWatch.why: Still the one live catalyst on the list, and still the one entry the rulebook explicitly forbids today. UPST reported 8/4 after the bell and is bid 32.05 at 11:22 ET against a 30.32 close, about +5.7%. That is the reaction day itself, which checklist item 2 calls a wait signal. The second hour faded it from the 32.36 bid at 10:22 back through the 32.23 open bid, so the intraday sequence is 33.81 after-hours, 32.23 open, 32.36, now 32.05 - a reaction day leaking, which is an argument for the day-2/3 pullback setup and against buying anything today. A fading spike is not a pullback; a pullback is a session that opens after the reaction day and holds.

entryWatch.trigger: Leader gapped down, most of the list red, only catalyst is a reaction-day spike
entryWatch.why: The branch the open resolved to and the position the account is still in two hours later. Eight of the nine candidates are now red at 11:22 - SOUN has flipped from +0.5% to -0.6%, leaving OKLO at +0.2% as the only green name and the reaction-day spike as the only catalyst - and four of the nine report tonight. Nothing in the second hour changed a flag or opened a setup. A one-position account has no way to be wrong cheaply here, and deployable cash keeps for a setup that fits.
